analysis: The supplied units are base-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 17287-18813), which are test vectors for the prompt-contract with the gemma-4-26b-8bit model. They contain no executable code, credentials or authorization logic. The changed ranges per file_changes are elsewhere in the file, in the Qwen-like vectors near base lines 3024-4003 and the later ones near 43813-54138. The patch excerpt shows additional_context {enable_thinking:false} being added, with token counts and chain hashes changing (803->767 tokens, a block boundary removed, chain_hash values changed). Only the base text of unchanged-region vectors was supplied to me, so I could not directly verify the head-side edits. No changed lines fall in the supplied excerpts (17287-18813 is outside the changed base ranges). Security relevance: the prompt_contract_id, block boundaries and chain_hash feed the prefix-cache keying (T-041, TB-007), so a fixture or contract change must be matched by the production code in lockstep. A mismatch would risk cache-key divergence or cross-scope sharing. The additional_context field is a new request-visible parameter. I could not verify the producing code (Go coordinator or Swift provider), so how additional_context is bound into prompt_contract_id, and whether a consumer could set it to influence cache sharing or the template, remains an integration question. No concrete regression is identified from the supplied evidence. The remaining uncertainty is the unseen head-side patch and the code that consumes these fixtures.
